'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[Kwatar Daban Masara airstrike]]
***At least 50 civilians were killed by a [[Nigerian Air Force]] [[airstrike]] at a [[fish market]] in the village of Daban Masara, [[Borno State]], two days ago. The [[Nigerian Armed Forces|military]] has imposed a ban on fishing in the area due to allegations that [[Islamic State – West Africa Province|ISWAP]] was [[Finances of the Islamic State|using the sales]] of the fish to fund their operations. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/nigerian-air-force-kills-dozens-civilians-northeast-sources-2021-09-28/ (Reuters)]
*[[South Thailand insurgency]]
**Two police officers are killed and four others injured as their van is hit by a [[Improvised explosive device|roadside bombing]] in [[Chanae District]], [[Thailand]]. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2189091/bomb-under-road-kills-2-police-officers-injures-4 (Bangkok Post)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Mali]] accuses [[France]] of "abandoning the country" by reducing its [[French Armed Forces|forces]] in the fight against [[jihadist]] groups. In response to the remarks, France accuses Mali's [[military junta]] of "wiping their feet on the blood of French soldiers". [https://www.channel4.com/news/mali-accuses-france-of-abandoning-country-by-reducing-troops-fighting-jihadists (Channel 4)]
*Five [[Sudan]]ese security forces personnel are killed and a sixth is injured during clashes with an [[Islamic State|IS]]-linked group in [[Khartoum]]. Eleven [[terrorist]]s are arrested. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/five-sudanese-security-officers-killed-clash-with-is-linked-group-statement-2021-09-28/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2021 United Kingdom fuel panic buying]]
**[[Secretary of State for Defence|Defence Secretary]] [[Ben Wallace (politician)|Ben Wallace]] approves a request for 150 [[British Army|military]] tanker drivers to help deliver [[Motor fuel|fuel]] to [[petrol station]]s. The Petrol Retailers Association says that 37% of its 5,500 stations have run out of fuel. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-58724332 (BBC News)]
*The [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Department for Transport]] announces that it is seizing control of [[train operating company]] [[Southeastern (train operating company)|Southeastern]] beginning next month following a "serious breach" of financial conduct. An investigation found that around [[£]]25 million in taxpayer funding is currently unaccounted for. [https://news.sky.com/story/southeastern-operator-stripped-of-franchise-after-25m-serious-breach-12420202 (Sky News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Cumbre Vieja volcanic eruption]]
**[[Spain]] declares the island of [[La Palma]] a "disaster zone" as the [[Cumbre Vieja]] [[volcano]] continues to erupt and produce lava flows. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/spain-declares-volcano-hit-la-palma-disaster-zone-2021-09-28/ (Reuters)]
**Lava flows from the volcano have reached the [[Atlantic Ocean]] after nine days, causing a massive cloud, according to local residents. [https://www.reuters.com/world/lava-la-palma-volcano-reaches-ocean-creating-huge-cloud-reuters-witness-2021-09-28/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in India]]
****The Subject Expert Committee of the [[Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation]] will allow the [[Serum Institute of India]] to conduct trials of the [[Novavax COVID-19 vaccine]] in children between the ages of 7 and 11 years. [https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/serum-institute-gets-nod-to-start-covovax-trials-on-children-above-7-yrs-121092800950_1.html (''Business Standard'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]]ese [[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Yoshihide Suga]] announces that the [[state of emergency]] that was declared in April will end on September 30, with [[COVID-19]]-related restrictions to then be gradually eased. [https://www.npr.org/2021/09/28/1041086891/japan-to-lift-all-coronavirus-emergency-steps-nationwide (NPR)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports a record 2,236 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 91,775. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2021/09/29/singapore-crosses-the-2000-mark-of-covid-19-cases-for-the-first-time-as-five-seniors-die-from-virus-complications (''The Star'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Romania]]
****[[Romania]] reports a record 11,049 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,210,810. [https://www.rferl.org/a/romania-covid-infections-record/31482050.html (RFE/RL)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 852 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 205,531. [https://www.brusselstimes.com/news/eu-affairs/187013/russia-hits-record-daily-covid-deaths/ (''The Brussels Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Serbia]]
****[[Serbia]] reports a record 8,467 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 926,269. [http://www.tanjug.rs/full-view_en.aspx?izb=686092 (Tanjug)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
****[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] reports a record 867 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, including 149 cases not previously reported due to technical issues. [https://www.9news.com.au/national/coronavirus-victoria-latest-case-numbers-867-new-infections-september-28-149-cases-not-reported-due-to-technical-glitches/32ad2d0a-291b-4f2e-bbc9-36e2cc194b26 (9 News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Costa Rica]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Costa Rica]]
***[[Costa Rica]] mandates that all state workers must be [[vaccination|vaccinated]] against COVID-19 despite not specifying a deadline, making it the first [[Latin America]]n country to impose a vaccination mandate. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/costa-rica-mandates-covid-19-vaccination-all-state-workers-2021-09-28/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Australia–Nauru relations]], [[Pacific Solution]]
**[[Australia]] and [[Nauru]] announce that, last week, they renewed their agreement to maintain a [[Nauru Regional Processing Centre|detention center]] in Nauru for [[asylum seeker]]s and [[refugee]]s who are attempting to reach Australia. Australia has provided millions of [[Australian dollar|dollars]] in order to maintain the offshore detention center. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/452490/australia-and-nauru-renew-commitment-to-detention-centre (RNZ)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital Gazette shooting]]
**Jarrod Ramos is sentenced to [[life in prison]] for the June 2018 murders of five employees in a [[mass shooting]] at Capital Gazette in [[Annapolis, Maryland|Annapolis]], [[Maryland]], [[United States]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/crime/capital-gazette-shooter-sentenced-to-life-in-prison/ar-AAOUUfr?ocid=msedgntp (MSN)]
*[[September 2021 Guayaquil prison riot]]
**Twenty-four people are killed and 42 others are wounded during [[prison riot|a battle]] between rival [[Prison gang|gangs]] at a prison in [[Guayaquil]], [[Ecuador]]. Some of the inmates were armed with guns and [[grenade]]s. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/29/at-least-24-killed-in-ecuador-prison-gang-clash-police (Al Jazeera)]
*Twenty-five people are injured, four critically, during an explosion at a block of flats in [[Gothenburg]], [[Sweden]]. An accident has been ruled out, with authorities suspecting a criminal background. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/sep/28/explosion-at-block-of-flats-in-gothenburg-sweden (''The Guardian'')]
*In a 35-page report, a commission appointed by the [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) to investigate sex abuses during the [[Ebola]] outbreak in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] finds that there were "clear structural failures" and "individual negligence" for the sex abuse and rape of women and girls between 2018 and 2020 by WHO staff. WHO director-general [[Tedros Adhanom]] apologizes for the abuses. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20210928-negligence-by-who-staff-to-blame-for-sexual-abuse-in-drc-independent-commission-says (France 24)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[NASA]] announces the scheduled launch of [[Lucy (spacecraft)|Lucy]], a twelve-year [[space probe]] on the [[Jupiter trojan]] [[asteroid]]s, the first mission to do so. It will launch from the [[Cape Canaveral Space Force Station]] in Florida on October 16. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/nasas-lucy-mission-to-probe-jupiters-mysterious-trojan-asteroids (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
